A1.justification: Both PDFs describe gen2seg, with the same models, losses, and principal experiments. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original segmentation and edge-detection results, training-data comparisons, ablations, robustness tests, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds quantitative Pascal-Part results and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: The instance-coloring losses, Stable Diffusion and MAE adaptations, and point-prompting procedure remain unchanged. The new part-grouping evaluation does not introduce a documented method component.

E1.justification: v3 adds Pascal-Part evaluation using PASCAL VOC 2012 part annotations across 16 object classes. This extends quantitative coverage to within-object grouping while retaining the existing training datasets, five segmentation benchmarks, and BSDS500.

E2.justification: The new Pascal-Part comparison introduces a No Compositionality baseline, computed from each part mask and its whole-object mask, alongside MAE-H, SD, and SAM. Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: The added Pascal-Part study evaluates part-mask IoU by object class against a whole-object control. Existing evaluation settings remain unchanged; the added iShape annotation-format statement is a disclosure, not evidence of a revised protocol.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds a quantitative test of emergent part grouping, previously illustrated qualitatively. Figure 4 adds a person-and-elephant prompting example, and Figure 5 adds a COCO annotation-noise example. Existing loss, timestep, color-perturbation, and finetuning-depth analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for these results. Table 7's new boldface identifies improvements of at least five IoU points, not statistical significance.

E6.justification: v3 adds Pascal-Part scores: for person, No Compositionality, MAE-H, SD, and SAM obtain 9.2, 27.3, 31.0, and 54.1 IoU, respectively. SAM exceeds both learned variants in every reported class. Existing numerical results remain unchanged, including the edge AP values moved from v2 Table 3 into v3 Figure 5; Figures 4 and 5 add qualitative outputs.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–7 are unchanged, and neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs. Applying ordinary IoU to the new part-grouping comparison adds no mathematical derivation or formal property.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about generative priors, generalization from restricted mask supervision, detailed boundaries, and emergent compositionality. The new study supports an existing claim rather than redefining the central contributions.

C2.justification: The new Pascal-Part discussion identifies class-dependent evidence of part grouping and proposes that whole-object supervision may overwrite part-level knowledge for training categories. Existing explanations of small-object failures, background grouping, and generative boundary priors remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 newly specifies PNG Cityscapes-style annotations for iShape. The abstract replaces its explicit pretrained-model availability statement with a reference to qualitative figures, code, and a demo; this does not establish that checkpoints were withdrawn. Existing implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Chen et al. (2014) for Pascal-Part and removes Zhu et al. (2017). Section 3.1 replaces the explicit statement claiming no novelty for the finetuning strategy with an acknowledgment of shared intuition with the same clustering-loss predecessors.

P1.justification: Localized prose, caption, and cross-reference edits accompany the new analysis, and the existing qualitative gallery gains an Appendix E heading. Most prose and the main section sequence remain unchanged. Section 4.4 introduces an incorrect Table 5 reference to results now displayed in Figure 5.

P2.justification: Figure 1 gains spacing between panels, Figure 4 gains a third example, and the edge-results table becomes Figure 5 with an accompanying visual comparison and reformatted scores. A new Pascal-Part Table 7 is added, while existing appendix figures and tables are repositioned and renumbered.

improvement.justification: Table 7 gives v2's visually supported compositionality claim a quantitative test with a whole-object baseline and SAM reference, strengthening the evidence and exposing class-dependent limitations. The annotation clarification and added examples also help. The gain is limited by sparse documentation of the part-evaluation procedure and the new incorrect cross-reference in Section 4.4.
